title: Basic Linear Regression — Quiz
description: Ten source-grounded questions spanning correlation, fitting, inference, residual diagnostics, CAPM, and matrix form.

questions.question: What does r=0 measure?
questions.explanation: The chapter’s y=x^2 example has r=0 despite a perfect nonlinear relationship. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

questions.question: For Wisconsin Lottery data, which fitted line is reported?
questions.explanation: The least-squares estimates reported are intercept 469.7 and slope 0.647. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

questions.question: What is R-squared?
options: Error SS divided by Total SS
The proportion of variability explained by the regression line
questions.explanation: R-squared is Regression SS divided by Total SS, hence explained variation; Error SS/Total SS is its complement. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

questions.question: Why does MSE divide Error SS by n-2?
options: Two coefficients determine a basic line
questions.explanation: A line needs an intercept and slope, leaving n-2 error degrees of freedom. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

questions.question: What happens to se(b1) if x values become more spread out, all else equal?
questions.explanation: se(b1)=s/[s_x sqrt(n-1)], so larger s_x reduces the standard error. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

questions.question: Which test addresses the importance of one explanatory variable?
questions.explanation: If beta1=0, x drops out of the basic model; that is the chapter’s t-test formulation. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

questions.question: What does a prediction interval cover that a confidence interval for the slope does not?
questions.explanation: Prediction adds uncertainty from a new observation, whereas the slope confidence interval targets beta1. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

questions.question: Which is a model-misspecification issue listed in residual analysis?
questions.explanation: The chapter lists lack of independence, heteroscedasticity, relations with explanatory variables, nonnormality, and unusual points. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

questions.question: In the CAPM example, what does a slope greater than one indicate?
questions.explanation: The text labels slopes greater than one aggressive and slopes less than one defensive. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

questions.question: What is the basic matrix regression representation?
questions.explanation: The technical supplement obtains the standard compact regression notation y=X beta+epsilon. A tempting alternative appears elsewhere in the chapter but does not answer this definition.
sources: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex
